dedupe_keys.name: machine learning to improve understanding of sewer pipe failures

description: Ehsan Kazemi and colleagues at the University of Sheffield describe a machine-learning model for interpreting linked sewer-pipe asset and failure data. The conference abstract states that random forests predict whether a pipe is at risk of failure and that the resulting probabilities can guide proactive inspection. It is a documented statistical infrastructure model; the deposit does not establish a downloadable implementation. Zenodo supplies the conference paper freely under CC BY 4.0, which applies to the paper. Geographic coverage, training-set size, feature definitions, split strategy and numerical accuracy are absent from the brief native description. Related Co-UDlabs records concern physical defect and inspection experiments, without a proven shared training set. A limitation is that the source only claims high accuracy without a value or independent validation details. No paper body, code or asset-level data were obtained.
